title: Ummah
def: The community of Muslims, united by faith across nations and cultures.
what: The Quran calls the Muslims a “middle” or balanced community (2:143), and says that “this community of yours is one community” (21:92). A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari compares the believers, in their mutual love and mercy, to one body: if one part suffers, the rest respond with sleeplessness and fever.
At the same time the Quran affirms diversity: peoples and tribes were made so that they should come to know one another, and the most honoured is the most God-conscious (49:13).
misread: That the ummah is a political bloc seeking to dominate the world.
sources: The ummah is a community of faith and ethics. Muslims live in states of every kind and have fought and allied with one another and with non-Muslims for every reason. The word is also used in the Quran for other peoples with their own prophets (10:47), which shows it is not a political claim.

title: Ummi
def: The Prophet is called ummī, “unlettered”, and the Quran uses ummiyyūn for the unlettered and for gentiles.
what: “Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet” (7:157). The Quran tells the Prophet: “You did not recite any book before it, nor write it with your right hand; otherwise those who follow falsehood would have doubted” (29:48). The Prophet said: “We are an unlettered nation; we do not write or calculate” (Sahih al-Bukhari), speaking of the Arabs. In 3:75 some of the People of the Book say “there is no blame on us in regard to the ummiyyīn”, a term for those who are not Jews.
misread: That the Prophet could not have known the stories of earlier prophets.
sources: Muslims see the Prophet’s unlettered state as part of the sign of the Quran: it was not a work of a scholar. Some scholars say ummī means “from the Mother of Cities”, Mecca, or “of the nations”, and the sense is not disputed that he had no formal training in scripture.
